questions.q: A car covers the first half of the distance between two places at 40 km/h and another half at 50 km/h. The average speed of the car is
questions.explanation: For equal distances, average speed = $\dfrac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2}=\dfrac{2\times40\times50}{90}=44.44$ km/h.

questions.q: The velocity of a particle moving along x-axis is given as $V=x^2-5x+4$ (in m/s) where x denotes the x-coordinate of the particle in metres. The magnitude of the acceleration of the particle when the velocity of the particle zero is
questions.explanation: $a=v\dfrac{dv}{dx}$. Since v = 0 at the instant considered, a = 0 regardless of dv/dx.

questions.q: Two stones begin to fall from rest from the same height, with the second stone starting to fall 'Δt' seconds after the first falls from rest. The distance of separation between the two stones becomes 'H', 't$_0$' seconds after the first stone starts its motion. Then t$_0$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $H=\tfrac12g t_0^2-\tfrac12 g(t_0-\Delta t)^2 = g\Delta t\, t_0-\tfrac12 g\Delta t^2$, so $t_0=\dfrac{H}{g\Delta t}+\dfrac{\Delta t}{2}$.

questions.q: A body is moving along a straight line with initial velocity v$_0$. Its acceleration a is constant. After t seconds, its velocity becomes v. The average velocity of the body over the given time interval is
questions.explanation: Average velocity = (v+v$_0$)/2. Since at = v − v$_0$, $\dfrac{v^2-v_0^2}{2at}=\dfrac{(v-v_0)(v+v_0)}{2(v-v_0)}=\dfrac{v+v_0}{2}$, matching option C.

questions.q: The displacement 'x' (in metre) of a particle of mass 'm' (in kg) moving in one dimension under the action of a force, is related to time 't' (in sec.) by, $t=\sqrt{x}+3$. The displacement of the particle when its velocity is zero, will be

For a body moving along a straight line, the following v-t graph is obtained: velocity rises linearly from an initial value to a higher value during a time interval (uniform acceleration), then stays constant at that higher value for an equal time interval (uniform motion). According to the graph, the displacement during
options: Uniform acceleration is greater than that during uniform motion.
Uniform acceleration is less than that during uniform motion.
Uniform acceleration is equal to that during uniform motion.
questions.explanation: Displacement = area under v-t graph. During uniform acceleration the velocity is lower on average (rising from a lower value) than during the following uniform-motion phase at the higher constant velocity, over the same time interval, so the displacement is less.

questions.q: A particle starts from rest. Its acceleration 'a' versus time 't' is shown in the figure: acceleration decreases linearly from a = 8 ms$^{-2}$ at t = 0 to a = 0 at t = 10 s. The maximum speed of the particle will be:
questions.explanation: Maximum speed = area under the a-t graph = $\dfrac{1}{2}\times 10\times 8 = 40$ ms$^{-1}$.

questions.q: At a metro station, a girl walks up a stationary escalator in 20 sec. If she remains stationary on the escalator, then the escalator takes her up in 30 sec. The time taken by her to walk up on the moving escalator will be
questions.explanation: Her speed is $L/20$, the escalator's speed is $L/30$; combined speed $=L/20+L/30=L/12$, so time $=12$ s.

questions.q: [Graph shows velocity v (y-axis) versus position x (x-axis) for a particle moving along a straight line: v decreases linearly from a positive value at x = 0 to zero at some x] The given graph shows the variation of velocity (v) with position (x) for a particle moving along a straight line. Which of the following graphs shows the variation of acceleration (a) with position (x) ? [Options A-D are small graphs of acceleration a versus position x with different linear shapes]
options: a decreases linearly from a positive value at x = 0 to zero, all in the positive-a region
a is constant (a horizontal line) for x > 0
a is a straight line that starts at its most negative value at x = 0 and rises linearly to zero at the same x where v becomes zero
a is a straight line rising from zero at x = 0 to a positive value, then continuing to rise
questions.explanation: Since v is linear in x, $v = v_0(1-x/x_m)$, so $dv/dx$ is a negative constant; then $a = v\\,dv/dx$ is linear in x, starting at its most negative value at x = 0 and rising to zero at $x=x_m$, matching the KEA key's chosen graph.

questions.q: A particle shows distance-time curve as shown in the figure [an S-shaped curve rising from P near the origin, through Q, then more steeply through R, and flattening near S at the top]. The maximum instantaneous velocity of the particle is around the point
questions.explanation: Instantaneous velocity is the slope of the distance-time graph, which is steepest around R on this curve; the KEA key accepted both P and C(R) as correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q: A car moving with a velocity of 20 ms$^{-1}$ is stopped in a distance of 40 m. If the same car is travelling at double the velocity, the distance travelled by it for same retardation is
questions.explanation: For constant retardation, stopping distance $s \propto v^2$. Doubling velocity quadruples the distance: $4 \times 40 = 160$ m.

questions.q: A body falls freely for 10 sec. Its average velocity during this journey (take g = 10 ms$^{-2}$)
questions.explanation: Average velocity for free fall from rest = $\dfrac{1}{2}gt = \dfrac{1}{2}(10)(10) = 50$ ms$^{-1}$.

questions.q: The velocity–time graph for two bodies A and B are shown. Then the acceleration of A and B are in the ratio [Graph: two straight lines from the origin; line A makes 25° with the time axis, line B makes 40° with the velocity axis (i.e. 50° with the time axis).]
questions.explanation: Acceleration equals the slope of the v-t graph. Line A makes 25° with the time axis (slope tan25°) and line B makes 40° with the velocity axis, i.e. 50° with the time axis (slope tan50°); ratio = tan25° : tan50°.

questions.q: A car moves from A to B with a speed of 30 kmph and from B to A with a speed of 20 kmph. What is the average speed of the car?
questions.explanation: Average speed = 2v$_1$v$_2$/(v$_1$+v$_2$) = 2\times30\times20/50 = 24 kmph.

questions.q: A body starts from rest and moves with constant acceleration for t s. It travels a distance x$_1$ in first half of time and x$_2$ in next half of time, then
questions.explanation: x$_1$ = \dfrac{1}{2}a(t/2)^2 = at^2/8; total distance in t is at^2/2, so x$_2$ = at^2/2 - at^2/8 = 3at^2/8 = 3x$_1$.

questions.q: A person throws balls into air vertically upward in regular intervals of time of one second. The next ball is thrown when the velocity of the ball thrown earlier becomes zero. The height to which the balls rise is ..... (Assume, g = 10 ms$^{-2}$)
questions.explanation: Time to reach the top equals 1 s, so v = g t = 10 m/s; height h = v$^2$/(2g) = 100/20 = 5 m.

questions.q: The displacement-time graphs of two moving particles make angles of $30^0$ and $45^0$ with the X-axis. The ratio of their velocities is ..................... [Graph: displacement on the Y-axis, time on the X-axis; one line makes $45^0$ with the time-axis, the other makes $30^0$]
questions.explanation: Velocity equals the slope of the displacement-time graph, so $v_1:v_2 = \tan30^0:\tan45^0 = (1/\sqrt3):1 = 1:\sqrt3$.

questions.q: A train is moving slowly on a straight track with a constant speed of 2 ms$^{-1}$. A passenger in that train starts walking at a steady speed of 2 ms$^{-1}$ to the back of the train in the opposite direction of the motion of the train. So to an observer standing on the platform directly in front of that passenger, the velocity of the passenger appears to be .................
options: 2 ms$^{-1}$ in the opposite direction of the train
questions.explanation: Velocity relative to ground $=$ train's velocity $+$ passenger's velocity relative to train $= 2 + (-2) = 0$.

questions.q: A motorboat covers a given distance in 6 hours moving downstream on a river. It covers the same distance in 10 hours moving upstream. The time it takes to cover the same distance in still water is .....................
questions.explanation: With boat speed $b$ and stream speed $s$: $b+s=d/6$, $b-s=d/10$. Solving gives $b=2d/15$, so time in still water $=d/b=7.5$ h.

questions.q: A body of mass 'm' moving along a straight line covers half the distance with a speed of $2\ \text{ms}^{-1}$. The remaining half of the distance is covered in two equal time intervals with a speed of $3\ \text{ms}^{-1}$ and $5\ \text{ms}^{-1}$ respectively. The average speed of the particle for the entire journey is
questions.explanation: For distance $d$: time for first half $= d/4$; if each equal time interval is $T$, $3T+5T=d/2 \Rightarrow T=d/16$; total time $=3d/8$, so average speed $= d/(3d/8) = 8/3\ \text{ms}^{-1}$.
